stem: A city replaces its diesel buses with electric buses to cut its greenhouse gas emissions. Under the definitions in RA 9729, this action is an example of what?
hints: Ask: is the city reducing a cause of climate change, or adjusting to its effects?
Section 3 of RA 9729 defines both adaptation and mitigation. Only one of them is about greenhouse gas emissions.
Adaptation is adjustment "in response to actual or expected climatic stimuli or their effects." The other term is human action on emissions. Decide which one fits the buses.

solution.methodName: Match the term to its legal definition

steps.action: Recall the definition of mitigation in Section 3 of RA 9729, as amended by RA 10174: "human intervention to reduce anthropogenic emissions sources and enhance removals by sinks of all GHG."
steps.why: Anthropogenic means caused by human activity (Section 3(c)). GHG means greenhouse gases, the gases that trap heat and warm the Earth.

steps.action: Compare with adaptation: "the adjustment in natural or human systems in response to actual or expected climatic stimuli or their effects."
steps.why: Adaptation copes with the effects of climate change. Mitigation reduces its cause.

steps.action: Apply it: switching to electric buses cuts greenhouse gas emissions from human activity. That is mitigation.

trapNotes.Adaptation: Adaptation means adjusting to the effects of climate change. The buses cut emissions, which tackles a cause, so this is mitigation.
trapNotes.Climate variability: Climate variability means variations in the climate itself (Section 3). It is not an action that anyone takes.
trapNotes.Vulnerability: Vulnerability is how easily a system is harmed by climate change (Section 3). It is a condition, not an action.

sourceRef.citation: RA 9729, Section 3, as amended by RA 10174 (definitions of adaptation and mitigation)
